QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_15

question.text: 'Theory of Change' (ToC) in the context of Logic Model design MOST closely refers to:

answer.text: A government schedule of eligible CSR activities

An articulated causal chain from inputs through activities, outputs, outcomes to impact — with explicit assumptions at each link — that explains HOW and WHY the intervention is expected to produce the desired change

explanation.text: The Logic: ToC expresses the causal logic behind the project: how inputs + activities, under stated assumptions, generate outputs -> outcomes -> impact. It is the narrative version of the Logic Model and surfaces assumption mapping at each causal link. The SIA tests ToC by examining whether each arrow in the chain is evidenced and whether the assumptions beneath it are plausible. The Trap: A, B, D are thematic distractors (pledge template, CSR Schedule VII, audit programme) that sound adjacent but miss the causal-chain essence of ToC. Cross-Exam Context: ToC is tested in XXIII Ch 5, referenced in SAS-1100 and SAS-1300, and parallels logic-of-intervention checks in CSR Section 135 evaluation (X-A Investment Adviser). Assessor's Pro-Tip: When reading the SE's ToC narrative, underline every 'will lead to' and 'therefore'. Each such phrase hides an assumption — ask the SE to state it explicitly in the LFM assumptions column.
